adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the test. Looking at the spec at line 43, the test stubs `TopicEmbed.expects(:topic_id_for_embed).returns(nil)` which triggers the else branch in the controller that calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. However, the test is mocking `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`. The actual controller code enqueues a job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` which internally calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`. The test appears to be incorrectly structured - it's testing synchronous behavior when the controller actually enqueues an async job. However, looking more carefully at the test setup with mocks, the test will pass because the mocks are set up, but the assertions may not actually verify the intended behavior since the job is enqueued asynchronously. The finding claims the test 'cannot verify the asynchronous retrieval behavior' which is partially correct, but the test will still pass due to how the mocks are set up. The test renders 'loading' template and returns success. The finding overstates the issue - the test does pass, it just doesn't deeply verify the async job execution.
